question: Show how the area under y = x^2 from 0 to 2 is approached by Riemann rectangles.

slides.title: The Region
slides.caption: y=x^2,\qquad 0\le x\le 2
slides.narration: We want the area under the curve y equals x squared from x equals zero to x equals two.

slides.title: Equal Widths
slides.caption: \Delta x=\frac{2-0}{n}=\frac{2}{n}
slides.narration: Divide the total interval length, which is two, into n equal pieces. Every rectangle has width two over n.

slides.title: Choose the Midpoints
slides.caption: x_k^*=0+\left(k-\frac12\right)\frac{2}{n}=\frac{2k-1}{n},\qquad k=1,2,\ldots,n
slides.narration: For each subinterval, use its midpoint to choose the rectangle height. The kth midpoint is its left endpoint plus half a rectangle width.

slides.title: Build the Sum
slides.caption: A_n=\Delta x\sum_{k=1}^{n}f(x_k^*)=\frac{2}{n}\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left(\frac{2k-1}{n}\right)^2
slides.narration: Each rectangle contributes its width times its midpoint height. Adding all n contributions gives the midpoint Riemann sum.

slides.title: Two Rectangles
slides.caption: A_2=\frac{2}{2}\left[\left(\frac12\right)^2+\left(\frac32\right)^2\right]=2.5
slides.narration: With two rectangles, the midpoints are one half and three halves. Their combined area is 2.5 square units.

slides.title: Four Rectangles
slides.caption: A_4=\frac{2}{4}\left[\left(\frac14\right)^2+\left(\frac34\right)^2+\left(\frac54\right)^2+\left(\frac74\right)^2\right]=2.625
slides.narration: Now use four rectangles. They are narrower, so the curved boundary is followed more closely, and the approximation rises to 2.625 square units.

slides.title: Eight Rectangles
slides.caption: A_8=\frac{2}{8}\sum_{k=1}^{8}\left(\frac{2k-1}{8}\right)^2=2.65625
slides.narration: With eight rectangles, the approximation is 2.65625 square units, even closer to the true area.

slides.title: Sixteen Rectangles
slides.caption: A_{16}=\frac{2}{16}\sum_{k=1}^{16}\left(\frac{2k-1}{16}\right)^2=2.6640625
slides.narration: With sixteen rectangles, the tops nearly trace the curve, and the approximation is 2.6640625 square units.

slides.title: The Error Term
slides.caption: A_n=\frac{8}{3}-\frac{2}{3n^2}
slides.narration: The general midpoint sum simplifies to eight thirds minus two over three n squared. The missing area is exactly two over three n squared.

slides.title: Exact Area
slides.caption: \int_0^2x^2\,dx=\left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^2=\frac{2^3}{3}-\frac{0^3}{3}=\frac{8}{3}
slides.narration: Because x squared is continuous, its exact area is the definite integral from zero to two. Evaluating the antiderivative gives eight thirds square units.

slides.title: Convergence
slides.caption: \lim_{n\to\infty}A_n=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\frac{8}{3}-\frac{2}{3n^2}\right)=\frac{8}{3}
slides.narration: As n grows, n squared grows without bound, so the error term tends to zero. The midpoint sums therefore converge to eight thirds.

slides.title: Numerical Comparison
slides.caption: A_2=2.5,\quad A_4=2.625,\quad A_8=2.65625,\quad A_{16}=2.6640625,\quad \frac{8}{3}\approx2.6666667
slides.narration: The values rise from 2.5 to 2.6640625, while the exact area stays at about 2.6666667. The gap narrows as the number of rectangles increases.

slides.title: FINAL ANSWER
slides.caption: \boxed{\lim_{n\to\infty}A_n=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(\frac{8}{3}-\frac{2}{3n^2}\right)=\frac{8}{3}=\int_0^2x^2\,dx}
slides.narration: Using equal-width midpoint rectangles on the interval from zero to two, the approximation is eight thirds minus two over three n squared. As n increases, this converges to eight thirds, the exact area under y equals x squared, measured in square units.
